cues.en: With that all out of the way, we learned a bit more about bindings, about binding to different kinds
of elements, about binding to custom components, binding to a value there, which is then output in
a form control or binding to the component itself.
Just as you can bind to any HTML element with the help of bind this which gives you access to the complete
element or the complete component where you can then read values or even interact with it.
Though as I mentioned, interaction is discouraged, or at least in most cases it's discouraged.
I also had a brief look at input validation.
And there the core takeaway is that Svelte has no built in validation, support or form validation support
You can use certain third party packages, but generally you have to write and build your own logic.
